title: reputation.py Phase B: EMA decay and operational-consequence engine BEHIND AN ACTIVATION FLAG
description: Build the coupling the valley has and PR-060 permits: EMA reputation decay feeding claim priority ordering, iteration bounds and worker slot allocation - OPERATIONAL parameters only, exactly the three PR-061 names. NO STAKING (D-17: no asset boundary). The engine ships with activation OFF and a guard test asserting it cannot activate while PR-061's authority is unresolved; constitutional parameters (decay rate, weights, thresholds) read from an operator-owned file that agents cannot legislate.

notes.note: HANDOFF -> verifier: T-420 built: the Phase B constitutional gate. Design: under D-17 the only boundary any agent cannot cross is the operator's off-machine private key, so activation and constitutional parameters live ONLY in .harness/constitutional/reputation.json + detached ssh signature, verified against the enrolled trust anchor (warrant.check_anchor reused as-is; NEW namespace harness-constitutional, never harness-warrant). dispatch (the one consequence verb) refuses unless the file VERIFIES and says activation on, and takes half-life/weights from the signed payload only; --half-life-days on dispatch is refused outright even when it agrees with the file. rank stays a consequence-free report, accepts trial params, labels them ratified/NOT RATIFIED. audit-immunity rewritten: the hardcoded six-True PASS dict is gone; it now reports mechanical figures (file state, activation, signed vs default params) and labels the rest NOT MECHANICALLY EVALUABLE with reasons, NO verdict (currency.py precedent). Evidence: pytest .harness/tests/test_reputation_phase_b.py -q -> 28 passed (was 6); full suite 786 passed, 4 skipped. Attack tests use REAL keys: absent/unsigned/wrong-key/wrong-namespace/tampered/activation-off/unenrolled all refuse; signed weights provably reach the score (3x weight -> 3x score); AST test pins the exhaustive map of write-capable calls to exactly one (allowed_signers rebuild in system temp dir) and that no ssh-keygen -Y mode other than verify appears. Zero-writes snapshot extended to every Phase B verb including activated dispatch. Bootstrap: before enrollment the gate is CLOSED (UNVERIFIABLE), not open. Files: .harness/bin/reputation.py, .harness/tests/test_reputation_phase_b.py. Verify hints: try to activate without the operator key; try to smuggle a param via CLI/env; check the AST map is exhaustive (not an allow-set that rots); check rank cannot be consumed as a gate.

VERIFIED (replay + adversarial attack, independent scratch keys, cognitive diversity via static diff + AST-mutation testing).

Adversarial attacks run against a scratch root + throwaway ed25519 keys (operator/mallory), never touching live .harness/trust or creating live .harness/constitutional:
1. Activation without operator key: signed constitutional file with attacker (mallory) key -> BAD_SIGNATURE, refused. Appended mallory's pubkey as a 2nd line in trust/root.pub (the classic append-attack) then signed with mallory -> caught by inherited warrant.check_anchor 1-key check ("TRUST ROOT TAMPERED: ... holds 2 keys"), refused.
2. Parameter smuggling: REPUTATION_ROOT env var vs --root (flag wins, correct precedence). Unknown weight key ("staking") in signed payload silently dropped, never reaches score (`if k in weights` allow-list) -- no asset/stake smuggling possible. Non-numeric weight value crashes with an uncaught ValueError (exit 1) rather than a clean refusal message -- noted as a minor robustness gap, NOT a security bypass since weights only ever come from the operator-signed file; no unauthorized dispatch output was produced. Activation values "ON","true","1","On",'"on"'," on","on " all correctly rejected (VERIFIED_OFF, exact string match only "on" activates). Missing "activation" key entirely -> VERIFIED_OFF (activation is None). --half-life-days and --half-life-days=45.0 (both agreeing and disagreeing with the file) refused outright on dispatch. Decoy file at constitutional/reputation_v2.json ignored (hardcoded single path, no glob).
3. Multiline root.pub attack: confirmed reputation.py inherits warrant.check_anchor's defense (see #1).
4. rank output (--json and text) inspected: no field states or implies authorization/activation; only informational constitutional_file_state + parameters_ratified, neither drives dispatch (verbs are independent processes, zero cross-verb state, confirmed by the AST no-write-outside-tempdir pin).
5. AST test non-vacuity, tested by copying reputation.py to a scratch dir and mutating the COPY only (live module untouched): injected a `Path(...).write_text` call into cmd_audit_immunity -> test_exhaustive_map_of_write_capable_calls' logic replayed against the mutant correctly flags 2 writers instead of the pinned 1. Injected `open(path,'w')` -> also caught. Mutated `-Y verify` to `-Y sign` -> test_no_code_path_can_sign's logic replayed against the mutant catches it (y_modes=['sign']). Appended a bare "harness-warrant" string literal -> test_the_warrant_namespace_is_never_borrowed's logic replayed against the mutant catches it. All four AST guards are non-vacuous.
6. Bootstrap posture: fresh unenrolled scratch root (no trust/) with NO constitutional file -> NOT_PRESENT, refused. Same root WITH a constitutional file signed by a real key but no anchor to check it against -> UNVERIFIABLE, refused. Gate closed by default in both cases, never silently open.

Compliance framing: grepped reputation.py for "safe"/"closed" claims -- none found; only conditional, mechanical VERIFIED/NOT_PRESENT/UNVERIFIABLE/BAD_SIGNATURE/VERIFIED_OFF states and NO VERDICT language in audit-immunity.

Static diff read (git diff 9eedc2d 2989a4e -- reputation.py): confirms the prior cmd_audit_immunity printed a literal hardcoded `{"status": "PASS", ...: True, ...}` dict with zero inputs read, and the prior cmd_dispatch had `"constitutional_immunity": {...,"status":"PASS"}` plus an unguarded `--half-life-days` CLI flag -- both are the exact defects T-420 claims to close, and the diff shows they are in fact gone, replaced by the gate described above.

One non-blocking observation for a future task: cmd_dispatch's `float(v)` on a signed-but-malformed weight value raises an uncaught ValueError/traceback instead of a clean refusal (operator-only input, not attacker-reachable, so not a gate bypass -- just an ungraceful failure mode worth hardening later).

No escape found in the constitutional gate itself. Housekeeping: lock.py status shows only main/T-418 locks (deliberate.py, test_deliberate.py), unrelated to T-420; lock.py sweep -> 0 expired locks.

REOPEN (was done): REOPENED by verifier-t421 (T-421 adversarial pass). Two BLOCKING escapes found in reputation.py Phase B; T-420's VERIFIED verdict does not hold against these.

(1) THE FLAG, TOCTOU capture -- activation flipped to "on" with NO operator signature over the activating payload, and the consequence verb's constitutional PARAMETERS (half-life, weights) forged, both while the ONLY legitimately signed file on disk says activation off. Root cause: _constitutional_status() reads the constitutional file TWICE, independently -- once via path.read_text() (parsed into st["payload"], which becomes the activation/weight decision) and again via a fresh open(payload_path,"rb") inside _verify_constitutional_signature() (what ssh-keygen actually verifies). Nothing ties the two reads to the same bytes. A concurrent process (any other agent on the shared OS user, D-17) that flips the file's content between the two reads gets: read #1 sees attacker payload (activation on, arbitrary weights/half-life) -> read #2 (after warrant.check_anchor's ssh-keygen -lf subprocess spawn, a multi-ms window) sees the file swapped back to the real operator-signed bytes -> ssh-keygen verifies successfully against the REAL bytes/sig -> module reports state VERIFIED, detail "signed by anchored root <real fp>" -> but returns st["payload"] from read #1, the attacker's forged dict. dispatch then runs with activation on and attacker-chosen constitutional parameters, never touched by any valid signature.

Reproduced against a scratch root with real throwaway ed25519 keys (never live .harness/trust or .harness/constitutional): a background thread doing os.replace() swaps between an "evil" (activation on, forged half-life 9999.0, forged rule_authorship weight 500.0, no valid signature) and the untouched "real" operator-signed bytes (activation off, the ONLY thing ever actually signed) while a tight loop calls `dispatch --candidates attacker --json` via the real CLI subprocess. Hit rate: 2/3 successful forged activations in one run, 1/1 on a second run forging arbitrary constitutional parameters. Control (no racer, static real file) correctly refuses every time with VERIFIED_OFF -- confirms the race, not a setup error, is what flips it.

Fix direction: read the payload bytes ONCE, feed those exact bytes to ssh-keygen -Y verify via stdin (subprocess.run(..., input=raw_bytes)) instead of re-opening the path a second time, and derive st["payload"] from that same buffer -- never two independent filesystem reads of one "verified" file.

(2) DECAY EVASION -- consolidations_achieved never decays. In _compute_phase_b_figures, decayed_f3 = float(f3.get("value", 0)) * w["consolidations"] has no call to _compute_ema_decay at all, unlike decayed_f1/f2/f4/f5 which all call it. consolidations carries the highest default weight (2.0) of the five components. Verified live: an identity with one precedent that reached the REITERATION_N=3 qualifying-applications threshold in 2020, with zero activity since, scores identically (2.0) at now=2026-08-30 and now=2030-08-30 (4 years / 48+ half-lives later at the 30-day default), while a comparable, separate identity that only self-published one fresh precedent decays from 0.9772 toward 0.0 over the same span. This directly contradicts the module's own stated purpose ("EMA Decay & Operational Consequences" engine, T-420 docstring) for its single highest-weighted component, and lets a dormant identity permanently outrank active ones in dispatch's claim-priority queue.
Reproduction script: <session-scratchpad>/decay_evasion_test.py

Static-file attacks the prior verifier already covered (wrong key, wrong namespace, tampered payload, activation off, unenrolled trust, root.pub append/swap, REPUTATION_ROOT env precedence, activation as non-string) were independently re-replayed by verifier-t421 with a fresh scratch root and all still correctly refuse -- those defenses hold. The escape is specifically the TOCTOU gap between the two independent reads, a vector neither the T-420 producer's note nor the pytest suite exercises (no test in test_reputation_phase_b.py runs concurrently against a live file-swap).

Full report, including the non-blocking self-dealing/inflation findings from family 1, is on T-421.

HANDOFF -> verifier: Round 2: both blocking escapes closed IN THE MECHANISM, plus two non-blocking hardenings folded in. (1) TOCTOU race (verifier's Family-3 escape): _constitutional_status now reads the payload bytes EXACTLY ONCE and threads them to _verify_constitutional_signature, which takes bytes (not a path) and verifies over them via ssh-keygen stdin. There is no second file read for check_anchor's subprocess to sit between, so no same-OS-user byte-swap can make a forged activated payload verify against genuine signed bytes. Tests: verify uses argument bytes even if the file is swapped to garbage; verifying tampered bytes fails even if the file is genuine; AST test pins _constitutional_status to exactly one read_bytes and zero open(); end-to-end swap-to-forgery returns BAD_SIGNATURE not the forgery. (2) Decay evasion (verifier's Family-2 escape): decayed_f3 (consolidations) now calls _compute_ema_decay per consolidated record's published_at, like f1/f2/f4/f5 -- a years-old consolidation no longer sits as a permanent non-decaying floor. Test: a 2020 consolidation's component decays to <5% after ~8 half-lives. (3) Non-blocking, folded in: rank/dispatch now print PHASE_B_CAVEAT (self-asserted identities / FORCE-IDENTITY-A open), matching Phase A's discipline; a non-numeric parameter in the signed file now refuses cleanly instead of raising uncaught ValueError. Family-1 (self-publish farming, Sybil across identity strings) is BOUNDED by PR-061 scope (operational-only, non-stakeable, D-17) and is the standing FORCE-IDENTITY-A gap, not newly opened here -- documented, not closed. Both mutants caught.

(2) Decay evasion, re-run decay_evasion_test.py against fresh scratch precedents: stale-farmer's 2020 consolidation now scores 0.0 (fully decayed) at both NEAR (2026-08-30) and FAR (2030-08-30) instead of a permanent 2.0 floor. Independently verified the decay is a real continuous curve (not just always-0/always-full): a consolidation 5 days old scores 1.7818, decays to 0.8909 at +30d (~half), 0.4454 at +60d (~quarter), 0.007 at +240d -- textbook EMA half-life behavior, confirming decayed_f3 now calls _compute_ema_decay per-record like f1/f2/f4/f5 (confirmed in diff).

Also verified: PHASE_B_CAVEAT prints on rank (text+json) and on dispatch (text+json, activated with a real signed file in a throwaway-key scratch root) -- 4/4 surfaces checked live. Non-numeric signed weight (weights.rule_authorship='banana', validly signed) -> clean 'refused: ... non-numeric parameter ...' on stderr, exit 1, no traceback.
